video.title: How Model Context Protocol (MCP) actually works
video.rationale: Covers: topic ✓ (0:04–1:34), CO1.LO1 ✓ (0:04–1:34) [from transcript] · Google Cloud Tech · tier 2 · 7:58 · 400,997 views · captions

Build an ADK agent with Google MCPs → https://goo.gle/4o6h8DP

APIs were built for deterministic programs, but AI models reason probabilistically. So how do you get your AI agents to talk to your tools and data without writing messy, custom integration code every time? Enter the Model Context Protocol (MCP). In this video, Smitha Kolan explains what MCP is, how it standardizes the way AI models discover and interact with external resources, and why it's becoming the new standard over traditional APIs for AI-powered applications

In this video, we dive deep into the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Architecture and break it down from first principles. 

We’ll cover:

The core building blocks of MCP → Host, Client, and Server
How they communicate and why the Client is essential
Real-world examples (GitHub, Slack, Google Drive)
The power of primitives: Tools, Resources, and Prompts
Standard operations like tools/list, resources/read, and more
The role of the Data Layer (JSON-RPC 2.0) and why it’s better than REST
The Transport Layer and how messages actually move between systems
